findings.detail: A ledger or status destination that is a hard link to a declared input passes the protection check. Writing the generated record then overwrites that live input. Likewise, two differently named hard links pass the distinct-destinations check, after which writing status destroys the ledger.
findings.evidence: render() compares resolved pathname strings at lines 240–243, then writes through existing files at lines 255 and 257. Path.resolve() resolves symbolic links but does not identify hard links sharing an inode. The destination tests cover identical paths only.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: hard-linked destinations bypass input protection

findings.detail: Declared executable inputs lose their executable permissions in the private copy. For example, a passing check.sh that invokes ./bin/check-subject encounters permission denied after materialization, so a valid plant campaign fails its baseline. The restored copy repeats the same problem.
findings.evidence: snapshot() retains only file bytes and their hashes. materialize() creates each file with write_bytes() at line 111 and never restores its mode. Both initial and restored trees use this function. The regression fixture invokes its non-executable shell inputs through Bash, so it does not exercise executable supporting files.
findings.title: Parallel paths: private copies discard executable input permissions

findings.detail: The skill now requires the runner for every variant, but the runner cannot represent the negative controls that the same skill requires to stay green. The documented formatter-ignore control must exit zero after planting; declaring that expected result is rejected, while declaring a nonzero result incorrectly fails the control. There is no supported branch for recording this required outcome.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md line 65 mandates the runner for every variant and line 68 mandates generated records. references/the-plant-table.md lines 44–50 explicitly require passing negative-control rows. checked-plant line 81 rejects a variant exit_code of zero, and its run and render gates require every row to have status red.
findings.title: Agent-prose control flow: mandatory runner cannot record required green controls

findings.detail: When a setup or check prints diagnostics and then times out, its captured stdout, stderr and final termination status disappear from results.json. Only the timeout exception's summary remains. This loses the failure evidence the checked runner promises to preserve.
findings.evidence: command() kills the process group, discards the final communicate() result and re-raises at lines 122–125. Consequently, check() never assigns that phase's result to the row. run_variant() records only the exception's string. The timeout regression asserts TimeoutExpired but does not assert retention of output or step status.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: timed-out steps lose captured evidence
